message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or agree on a different target). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when you finish a round. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a direction‑changing card is played). | | **Playing a card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard. If you have no playable card, you must draw from the draw pile. | | **Special cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction (acts like Skip if only two players).
• **Draw Two (+2)** – next player draws two cards and misses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and misses a turn (must be challenged if you suspect you could have played a matching card). | | **Drawing** | If you draw a playable card, you may immediately play it. Otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you’re down to one card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player calls it out before you play your second card, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a round** | The first player to get rid of all their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards still held by the other players:
• Number cards = face value
• Draw Two / Reverse / Skip = 20 points each
• Wild / Wild Draw Four = 50 points each
Points earned by the winner are added to their total. | | **Game end** | The first player to reach the agreed‑upon score (e.g., 500) wins the game. | **Optional house rules** (just pick one set before starting): 1. **Stacking** – Instead of drawing, a player can stack a +2 or +4 on top of a previous +2/+4, forcing the next player to draw the cumulative amount unless they also stack. 2. **No challenge** – Wild Draw Four can always be played regardless of whether the player could have matched the color. 3. **Draw‑to‑win** – A player who finishes a round with a Wild Draw Four must draw four cards before scoring. Enjoy!
